Hi Rajiv / Sofia,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Per request, quick recap of the pain, goals, and proposed next steps so we have an aligned reference. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of pain points we heard:
- Unpredictable inference latency and token cost with current multi-tenant endpoints during heavy overnight batch runs and peak daytime bursts.
- Data isolation requirements for PII processing (legal team requires tenancy isolation + audit logs).
- Occasional throttling from the current managed vendor during model retrains that reduces throughput during critical batch windows.

Current stack and constraints:
- Core stack: internal inference service (K8s + TFServing) fronting GPU instances on CloudInfra.
- Model: proprietary transformer (4.4B dense) with KV cache needs and persistent sessions for chat flows.
- Peak target: sustained 1200 tokens/sec aggregate across 3 endpoints, with spikes up to ~3k tokens/sec for up to 30 minutes during marketing campaigns.
- RPO/RTO: Recovery from node failure expected under 5 minutes; legal requires audit logs for inference requests for 90 days.

Success criteria (what would make this a win):
1) Predictable baseline throughput at or above 1.2k TPS with 95th percentile latency <= 150ms for 1k-token requests.
2) Logical and physical isolation for regulated workloads (dedicated capacity / VPC) and 90-day audit retention.
3) Autoscaling/burst behavior that supports 3k TPS spikes without manual provisioning and without violating latency SLOs.
4) Clear cost model for committed capacity + burst usage so finance can evaluate TCO versus current provider.

Recommended Redwood Dedicated fit and next steps:
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools) to provide predictable throughput and tenancy isolation. We recommend a baseline reserved pool sized for the 1.2k TPS steady-state with burst pool configured for automatic short-term scaling to cover 3k TPS spikes.
- Autoscaling policy options: time-windowed autoscale (fast ramp for 15–30min bursts with cooldowns) and manual throttle-based scaling for sustained increases. We will validate policy behavior in an architecture deep-dive with your SREs.
- Audit/compliance: Redwood Private control plane can deliver audit logs + KMS integration; will confirm retention and export cadence during SOC2 evidence exchange.

Attachments included: nimbus-mapping-reqs.xlsx (your notes from today), draft capacity quote (redwood-dedicated-capacity-quote.pdf).

Proposed immediate actions:
1) Schedule a technical architecture deep-dive with your SRE and model ops team — suggested attendees: Rajiv, Sofia, Elena (CloudInfra contact), Laura (our solutions engineer), and one of our infra architects. Can we aim for next week (Mar 3–5)?
2) I’ll share a draft committed-capacity quote + example autoscale configs for your finance/infra review.
3) If you can send any perf logs for a 24-hour period (sample 1h windows around peak), Laura can use those to create a more accurate sizing model.

Thanks — cc’ing Laura and Marissa to loop in solutions and CS.

Best,

3) Logging/retention: 90-day retention is required; do you support log export to our S3 (encrypted) for long-term storage? Also need confirmation on data access controls for audit requests.

Rajiv — appreciate the questions. Short answers inline below and happy to go deeper on the call Tuesday.

1) Burst provisioning: Redwood Dedicated supports a hybrid approach — warm standby instances (pre-warmed, minimal cold-start) for predictable short bursts and fast on-demand provisioning for larger sustained bursts. We typically recommend a small warm pool sized to cover the first 30–60s of spike traffic plus autoscale for the remainder. I’ll include example latency numbers and a proposed warm-pool sizing in the capacity doc.

2) Isolation: We offer three tenancy modes for Dedicated: logical isolation (dedicated pools within shared hosts), host tenancy (dedicated hosts but shared underlying hardware), and full hardware tenancy (physical GPU isolation). There are incremental cost deltas; full hardware tenancy is the most expensive but meets strict compliance requirements. I’ll surface comparative pricing in the quote PDF attached.

3) Logging/retention: Yes — audit logs can be exported to your S3 (server-side encrypted) on an automated cadence; we also offer a managed retention policy for 90/180/365 day buckets. Access controls can be role-based with RBAC mappings to your IDP for audit requests. We’ll include the exact export manifest and sample IAM policy in the follow-up docs.

Next steps confirmed:
- Deep-dive Tues Mar 3 11:00am PT (invite to follow).
- Laura will run initial sizing using the perf sample you upload; she’ll share a recommendation doc ahead of the call.
- I’ll send revised committed-capacity quote with warm-pool sizing and tenancy options by Monday EOD.

If anything else pops up, flag it here. Otherwise, see you on Tuesday.

Best,
